title: POC workload playback & burst modeling - Southridge
header: Date: 2025-08-06 | Start: 16:00 PDT | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Derek Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Rodriguez (Southridge Head of ML), Tom Brewer (Platform Eng), Aisha Khan (SRE)
summary: Kickoff to scope a 6-week POC: replay production traffic + burst modeling to validate SLA. Discussed QPS patterns, concurrency, token-length distributions, tail latency targets, security requirements (VPC, KMS, SOC2), and success criteria. Agreed next steps: SHARE sample workload, Redwood to draft benchmark plan and run initial small-scale replay, schedule in-zone benchmark week 3.
topics: Workload characterization: QPS, concurrency, token distribution
Burst/episodic traffic modeling and tail latency
Deployment choices: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC)
transcript: [00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick check — can you all hear me?
[00:05] Lina: Yes, good here. Sorry I'm on mobile, bit of background noise.
[00:08] Derek: Great — we'll run through scope and then dig into the traffic shape. We blocked 45 minutes for the technical part, then 10 for next steps.

[00:20] Tom: For context we run our conversational agent in prod with a mix of synchronous customer requests and async batch scoring. Baseline qps is low but we see fat bursts during campaign windows.
[00:34] Aisha: Important — our SREs care about 95th and 99th p99 latency, and also cold-start spikes when the traffic bursts hit.
[00:45] Maya: Perfect. Lina — what's your primary success criteria for the POC? Latency targets, cost, or accuracy?

[00:52] Lina: All three but priority order is reliability/latency, then cost predictability, then output quality. Specifically we want 95th < 300ms for typical prompts and p99 < 800ms for burst windows, otherwise auto-throttle. Open to adjusting if unrealistic.
[01:10] Derek: Noted. Can you give ballpark numbers for your bursts? Peak qps, duration, concurrency?

[01:18] Tom: Normal burst: 200 qps for 10-20 minutes during peak; extreme: 1200 qps sustained for ~60s when a campaign hits. Concurrency per request is usually 1, but we have async jobs hitting the same model — so effective concurrency sometimes ~150-200.
[01:40] Maya: Helpful. What about tokens — input vs output size distribution? Any long-form outputs?

[01:46] Lina: Inputs are short — mean ~24 tokens, 75th perc ~40. Outputs are variable: median 80 tokens, mean 120 but we have a long tail — 2-3% of requests generate >512 tokens and rare outliers to 2k tokens. Those long tails are what blow up cost and units.
[02:05] Derek: Good — that distribution matters. For cost and tail latency we'll recommend quantization + shorter context where feasible and prefix caching if you have repeated system prompts.
[02:13] Tom: We do reuse system prompts across many requests. Also we sometimes pass conversation history of up to 2k tokens for certain flows.
[02:22] Aisha: From infra perspective, we need VPC peering and customer-managed KMS. We can't send PII to hosted environments unless it's encrypted and we get SOC2 evidence.

[02:32] Maya: Understood. For the POC we can run in Redwood Dedicated in your cloud region or a private VPC install — both support KMS and audit logs. Derek, can you remind them about the data-flow for replay?

[02:40] Derek: Sure. Our normal POC flow: you provide an anonymized sample of production traffic (S3 link or replay harness). We run a small-scale warmup benchmark to estimate per-node throughput and tail latencies, then run scaled replay shaping bursts to match your peak qps and token mix. We'll collect latency quantiles, token counts, throughput, and compute cost projections.
[03:03] Lina: Timeline? We want this done before our Q4 campaign, ideally a 6-week pilot with in-cloud benchmarks in week 3.

[03:12] Maya: That's doable: week 0: scoping and sample handoff; week 1: env setup & small warmup runs; week 2: tuning and config; week 3: full replay/benchmark; week 4-5: validation and adjustments; week 6: wrap and report.
[03:27] Tom: One question — do you support per-customer routing so we can route high-priority customers to dedicated capacity?
[03:33] Derek: Yes, our smart routing allows rule-based routing by customer tier, region, or cost targets. Fallback policies available to route to a cheaper variant when dedicated is saturated.
[03:45] Lina: For benchmarks we care about token accounting for prompt+completion separately; can you break out cost per input vs cost per output and include KV cache hit rates?
[03:55] Derek: We can. We'll instrument token-level metrics and include prefix cache/KV cache hit rates. If you have a distribution of repeated prompts we can simulate cache warmup effects.
[04:10] Aisha: Security checklist — SOC2, SAML SSO, RBAC, KMS/HSM keys, audit logs retention (we need 1 year), and data residency in eu-west for EU customers. Do you have those?

[04:22] Maya: Yes — we have SOC2 Type II, SAML, RBAC controls, KMS integrations, and configurable audit log retention. We'll share our security pack. For residency we can deploy in eu-west or your VPC.
[04:34] Lina: Great. Also curious about batching — do you do adaptive batching that won't blow p95 under burst?

[04:40] Derek: Our runtime does continuous batching with latency SLOs: it will batch up to a configured max wait but will also enforce per-request latency SLOs. You can tune batching windows or opt out for low-latency flows.
[04:52] Tom: Are there model variants we should consider for cost/latency tradeoffs? Like quantized smaller models or distilled versions?

[04:58] Derek: Yes. For heavy volume we often recommend a quantized 4-bit variant for throughput with marginal quality drop. Also can serve a smaller model for inference fallback. We'll show quality regression numbers tied to prompt sets.
[05:12] Lina: On quality — we will run the Redwood eval harness vs our golden prompts. We expect >95% parity on NLU intents for the core flows.
[05:18] Maya: Good call — include that in the success criteria. Let's capture measurable success criteria now.

[05:23] Lina: Measurables: 95th < 300ms for normal traffic (up to 200 qps), p99 < 800ms in burst windows up to 1200 qps for 60s, cost projection within 20% of target, and quality parity >95% for golden prompts.

[05:39] Derek: We'll also add operational KPIs: KV cache hit rate >50% after warmup for repeated prompts, no more than 1% of requests falling back due to resource saturation, and labeling of error types in logs.
[05:51] Tom: For the replay dataset we can provide a 7-day rolling sample anonymized and a compressed replay trace. We'll include header info on token counts per request.
[05:59] Aisha: We'll need an NDA addendum for sharing sample data; legal is looped in and will sign the POC agreement.
[06:06] Maya: We'll send the POC template and security addendum after the call. Derek, can you outline the benchmark specifics so Lina can validate?

[06:12] Derek: Benchmark plan sketch: 1) small warmup: 10m @ 50% baseline to warm caches; 2) steady-state run at baseline qps for 30m to get p50/p95/p99; 3) burst tests: ramp to 200 qps and hold 20 mins, then stress test with 1200 qps spikes (3x 60s) to capture tail; 4) long-tail test: sample the 2-3% >512-token outputs to observe mem/kv effects. We'll collect latency quantiles, CPU/GPU utilization, tokens/sec per node, and cost estimates. We'll also run an A/B for quantized vs full precision models for a subset of traffic.
[06:48] Lina: That looks thorough. How do you simulate network variability? Our customers are global and some see high RTTs.
[06:55] Derek: We can inject synthetic RTTs and also run tests from your regions. If we deploy in your VPC, we'll use your NAT/GW path to reproduce real path characteristics.
[07:05] Tom: Anything we should pre-measure on our side?

[07:08] Maya: Please send: 1) anonymized replay trace (S3 link), 2) histogram of input/output token lengths, 3) list of golden prompts and expected labels, 4) target cost per 1M tokens if you have one, and 5) contact for infra access (IAM role or peering info).
[07:22] Lina: We'll get that to you by EOD Friday — legal permitting. Also note we may want dedicated in-region capacity during the campaign timeframe.
[07:31] Derek: We'll price dedicated capacity options in the proposal, including burst burst capacity for short windows and autoscale rules.
[07:38] Aisha: On observability — we need token-level traces and per-route dashboards; can Redwood provide those?
[07:44] Maya: Yes, the Redwood Console exposes per-route latency, token breakdown, tracing hooks, and cost per token. We'll grant access to a demo account for you to inspect.
[07:53] Tom: A note on tokenizer mismatches — we've seen tokenization differences across model families that change token counts by ~10-15%. Will you standardize on tokenizer for benchmark?

[08:02] Derek: We'll use the tokenizer consistent with the model variant in the POC and will run an adjustment pass if your current production uses a different tokenizer. We'll record tokens before and after to normalize cost numbers.
[08:16] Lina: Good. Any gotchas to watch for when we replay conversation history? Sometimes timestamps and session IDs cause duplicates leading to cache misses.
[08:24] Derek: For replay we strip unique session IDs and map repeated system prompts to consistent tokens to maximize cache realism. We'll provide a mapping script.
[08:33] Maya: Let's capture action items while we're fresh.
[08:36] Tom: Quick question: what's your expected minimum dataset size for meaningful results?
[08:41] Derek: For statistical significance on p99 we'd like at least 100k requests across the replay, but you can start small — we'll extrapolate cautiously.
[08:49] Lina: We can do 150k sample across 7 days. Legal will scrub PII.
[08:54] Maya: OK. Action items then — and timing. I'll read them out.
[09:00] Maya: Action: Redwood to send POC template + security pack — owner: Maya Chen — due: 2025-08-08.
[09:10] Maya: Action: Southridge to provide anonymized replay S3 link + token histograms + golden prompts — owner: Lina Rodriguez — due: 2025-08-08 (pending legal/nda).
[09:20] Derek: Action: Redwood SE to draft benchmark plan with exact scripts and replay config — owner: Derek Patel — due: 2025-08-10.
[09:29] Tom: Action: Southridge infra to share peering/IAM contact info for dedicated trial — owner: Tom Brewer — due: 2025-08-11.
[09:37] Aisha: Action: Legal to sign POC addendum / NDA — owner: Aisha Khan (coord with Legal) — due: 2025-08-08.
[09:44] Maya: We'll schedule the engineering kick on 2025-08-12 to start env setup, does that work?
[09:50] Lina: Yes that is fine.

[09:53] Derek: A few technical notes: 1) We'll measure warmup time for KV cache to reach steady-state hit rates; 2) For the 2-3% long outputs we may route to specialized instances to avoid blocking standard lanes; 3) We'll capture GPU mem pressure and token-cache churn.
[10:12] Tom: For cost modeling, can you provide per-hour pricing of dedicated nodes and estimated tokens/sec per node for the model variant?
[10:20] Derek: We'll include a per-node throughput table in the benchmark report and a cost projection sheet — expected tokens/sec depends on quantization and model, but we'll provide ranges.
[10:29] Maya: Competitors mentioned in chat: Vertex AI for managed endpoints and a self-hosted stack that another vendor offered. We'll include differentiation notes in the follow-up.
[10:36] Lina: Any questions from Redwood?
[10:39] Maya: Just one — during the POC do you want us to simulate synthetic multi-tenant load or use real per-customer traces?
[10:46] Tom: Real per-customer traces if possible — we want to see tenant skew effects.
[10:50] Derek: Ok we will add multi-tenant skew in the replay harness. We'll also provide scripts to vary token-length mix to test sensitivity.
[11:00] Aisha: On monitoring retention — can you ship raw traces to our S3 for our analysis?
[11:05] Maya: Yes — we can export raw telemetry to your S3 with encrypted transfer.
[11:10] Lina: Great. Last thing — can Redwood run a short 10-minute smoke run before the full replay so we can sanity-check metrics?
[11:16] Derek: Absolutely — smoke run scheduled day of full replay, we'll coordinate windows.
[11:21] Maya: OK we'll wrap here. Recap: send docs, receive data, schedule kickoff 8/12, full replay week 3, deliver report week 6.
[11:31] Lina: Thanks everyone, excited to get going.
[11:34] Tom: Thanks — will follow up with IAM details.
[11:36] Aisha: Thanks all.
[11:38] Maya: Bye everyone, we'll send the follow-up email in the next 24 hours.
[11:42] Speaker 1: (end of recording)
